test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The area of a rectangle increases by 7 m² if its length is increased by 6 m and breadth is decreased by 5 m. If the length is decreased by 6 m and breadth is increased by 7 m, then its area increases by 31 m². What is the perimeter of the original rectangle (in m)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **length** be L and **breadth** be B.

From given conditions: (L + 6)(B − 5) = LB + 7 ⇒ −5L + 6B = 37

And: (L − 6)(B + 7) = LB + 31 ⇒ 7L − 6B = 73

Adding equations: 2L = 110 ⇒ L = 55 m; Substituting L: 6B = 37 + 275 = 312 ⇒ B = 52 m

**Perimeter** = 2 × (55 + 52) = 2 × 107 = 214 m.

**∴ The correct answer is 214 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial **Area** = LB. Two conditions for change in dimensions.

**Formula:** **Area of rectangle** = Length × Breadth | **Perimeter** = 2(L + B)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/057e6747120d869877c0500c5aa626a83931961909bfeb4c696c98f8e7898991.png] 

**Case 1:** (L + 6)(B − 5) = LB + 7

⇒ LB − 5L + 6B − 30 = LB + 7

⇒ −5L + 6B = 37 ... (i)

**Case 2:** (L − 6)(B + 7) = LB + 31

⇒ LB + 7L − 6B − 42 = LB + 31

⇒ 7L − 6B = 73 ... (ii)

**Solving (i) and (ii):**

⇒ (−5L + 6B) + (7L − 6B) = 37 + 73

⇒ 2L = 110 ⇒ **Length** = 55 m

⇒ −5(55) + 6B = 37 ⇒ −275 + 6B = 37 ⇒ 6B = 312 ⇒ **Breadth** = 52 m

⇒ **Perimeter** = 2(55 + 52) = 2(107) = 214 m

**∴ The correct answer is 214 m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of Rectangle

Opposite sides are equal and parallel. All internal angles are 90°. **Diagonal** = √(L² + B²).

Percentage Change in Area

If length increases by x% and breadth increases by y%, net area change = [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Relationship between Perimeter and Area

For a given **perimeter**, a **square** (L=B) has the maximum **area** among all rectangles.</p
